title: Massive extended streamers feed high-mass young stars
question: Do high-mass protostars like G336 ALMA1 lack a large Keplerian disk and instead gain gas via massive streamers reaching well inside the expected disk radius, and are the flows strong enough to overcome stellar feedback?

data.sensitivity: continuum 28 uJy/beam; line cubes 1.1-1.3 mJy/beam per channel

what.value: Central mass 10 Msun, inclination 65 deg, outer streamer temperature 93 K, outer infall rate ~1e-4 Msun/yr

evidence.quote: A central mass of 10 ${\rm M}_\odot$ was determined by (cite: Olguin2023)
Assuming that the luminosity of the clump $L=2.5\times10^{4}$ ${\rm L}_\odot$ (cite: Urquhart2018)
$\kappa_{\nu}=1$ cm$^2$ g$^{-1}$ is the dust opacity at 1.3 mm (cite: Ossenkopf1994)

recipe.method: Combine C-8 and C-9 data, align channels with CVEL, phase-only self-calibration
GOCONTINUUM continuum separation; tclean continuum; YCLEAN line cubes
key_parameters: continuum robust 0.5, threshold 1.25 sigma; lines robust 2, multiscale 0,5,15,25

recipe.method: Gaussian fit to ALMA1 continuum within 50 mas radius
Mendoza2009 streamlines grid over centrifugal radius, polar and azimuthal angles, best chosen by visual inspection; separate inner blue streamer in mid-plane with r_f=200 au
key_parameters: rc 400-600 au (50 au steps), theta0 75-85, phi0 50-70; inner: r_c=200 au, theta0=89, phi0 140-195, v_r0=0.1 km/s selected
assumptions: Central mass 10 Msun, inclination 65 deg, mid-plane trajectory inside centrifugal radius

recipe.goal: Compare PV diagram with velocity distributions
recipe.method: Compare observed PV along blue streamer spine to Keplerian, Keplerian+free-fall, IRE (FERIA) and streamline models at deprojected radius
key_parameters: inclination 65 deg, P.A. disk -55 deg, centrifugal barrier 250 au

recipe.goal: Estimate masses, infall rates, timescales and forces
recipe.method: Optically thin dust mass; free-fall and viscous times; Mdot = v_ff M/l; force L/c vs Mdot v
key_parameters: T=100 K, kappa=1 cm2/g at 1.3 mm, R_dg=0.01, d=3.1 kpc, mu=2.33, alpha 0.1-1, v_ff=6 km/s, l=500 au
assumptions: Optically thin dust, dust-to-gas 0.01, Ossenkopf1994 opacity

evidence.quote: The resulting continuum angular resolution is $0.031\times0.025$” (P.A.=57.5$^{\circ}$; $96\times78$ au)
resulting in a geometric mean size of $39\pm6\,{\rm mas}$ (121 au)
The flux density of the Gaussian is $7.7\pm1.1$ mJy.
equally good matches can be obtained with a centrifugal radius between 450 and 550 au
The resulting masses are 0.24 ${\rm M}_\odot$ for the gas in ALMA1
0.6 ${\rm M}_\odot$ for the inner blue streamer
This gives infall rates of $1.6\times10^{-3}$ ${\rm M}_\odot$ yr$^{-1}$ and $0.9\times10^{-3}$
$0.9\times10^{-3}$ ${\rm M}_\odot$ yr$^{-1}$ for the inner blue and red-shifted streamers
the force exerted by the source radiation field is of the order of $10^{22}$ N
the force exerted by the inflow resulting from the blue-shifted streamer is of the order of $10^{24}$ N

not_stated_but_needed: Self-calibration solution intervals and number of iterations
Calibration pipeline version and flux calibrator
tclean image size, cell size and mask parameters
Streamline model fixed parameters not repeated from Olguin2023
Viscosity alpha and 100 K temperature choices beyond the justification given
missing_for_reproduction: Exact PV cut widths and paths
score_reason: Public data, released scripts and mostly explicit parameters; some calibration and imaging details missing, and streamline fits are visual.
rediscovery_reason: Public data, released scripts, numeric results (continuum fit, masses, infall rates) can be re-derived.
